answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity through work that cannot be faked cheaply: every agent must stake a small deposit and earn reputation slowly, like an opal forming layer by layer, so a flood of fresh identities starts with zero trust. When a new agent appears like a comet, bright but unproven, it can only transact in tiny amounts until its history accumulates. Attackers then face a rising tide of cost: each fake identity needs its own stake, its own slow history, and losing the stake on misbehavior makes mass forgery unprofitable.
